The main takeaway from our work is that

, in young children, meaning depends on variably elaborate visualization processes, integrating visuo-audio-motor experiences and multimodal embodying representations, and that these processes may be modulated by the abstractness of the word.

, similarly to adults, in young children meaning is not only a matter of language and semantics, but also of the body and the world, which is a key aspect for the development of language and cognition in general.
